title: Make decisions and reject bad input
outcome: Route urgent work while rejecting impossible counts.
story: Amina wants urgent messages at the top of her queue. She also wants the app to reject impossible numbers instead of quietly accepting them.

frames.explanation: A condition chooses a result when a rule is true.
A negative arrival count makes no sense. Validation rejects it before routing.
Valid ordinary work goes into the normal queue.

sections.title: A program can choose
paragraphs: A condition is a question with a true or false answer. Is this message urgent? Is this number below zero? An if instruction runs a block of code when its condition is true.

A boolean is a value that is either true or false. In our exercise, urgent is a boolean supplied by the lesson. Writing if (urgent) means: use this branch when urgent is true. A default result covers the other situation.

sections.title: Valid input comes first
paragraphs: Validation checks whether information is acceptable before a program uses it. A message count must be a whole number at least zero. A count of -2 is impossible. A count of 1.5 does not represent a whole message.

Number.isInteger(value) checks for a whole number in JavaScript. It also rejects text such as "2". The expression value < 0 checks for a negative number. We reject bad values before deciding whether the queue is urgent.

sections.title: More than one rule
paragraphs: The symbol || means or: reject the input if any listed problem is present. The symbol ! means not: !Number.isInteger(current) is true when current is not a whole number.

Order matters. First check the counts. Next check that answered is no larger than current + incoming. Only then choose urgent or normal. Otherwise a request could receive an urgent label even though its numbers are invalid.

sections.title: Write rules people can explain
paragraphs: A useful rule has a reason. Rejecting a negative arrival count protects the meaning of the data. Rejecting too many answered messages prevents a negative remaining count. Routing urgent messages helps Amina decide what to handle first.

Keep the result vocabulary small: normal, urgent, or invalid. A later interface can show a helpful message for each result. Test one example for every branch so a change to one rule does not accidentally remove another.

words.meaning: A true-or-false question used to choose an action.
Checking that input follows the rules before using it.

explanation: The default result starts as accepted.
The condition checks two problems: a non-whole number or a negative number.
The condition is true for -1, so the program changes result to invalid.

exercise.title: A safe queue rule
exercise.brief: Return normal, urgent, or invalid. Check the numbers before deciding the priority.

steps.title: Route urgent work
steps.task: Keep normal as the default. Change the result to urgent when urgent is true.

steps.title: Validate all three counts
steps.task: Reject negative or non-whole counts. An invalid request must stay invalid even when it is urgent.
steps.hint: Check Number.isInteger for each count and reject any count below zero. Put the priority rule in an else if branch.

steps.title: Protect the remaining count
steps.task: Reject a request that claims more answered messages than current + incoming.
steps.hint: Add answered > current + incoming to the invalid branch.

cases.label: Ordinary valid work
cases.why: The default branch should remain useful.

cases.label: Urgent valid work
cases.why: Urgency changes routing only after validation.

cases.label: Negative arrivals
cases.why: Invalid numbers must not be hidden by urgency.

cases.label: Text that looks like a number
cases.why: The contract expects a number, not text.

cases.label: Answering messages that do not exist
cases.why: The remaining queue cannot become negative.

cases.label: Exactly all messages answered
cases.why: A boundary can be valid: answering all three is allowed.

project.title: A queue rule Amina can trust
project.brief: Write a small decision service that accepts counts and an urgency flag, then returns one clear result.
deliverables: A decision program with three named results.
A table of valid and rejected inputs.
A customer-facing explanation for invalid input.

milestones.title: Route work
actions: Describe normal and urgent in plain English.

milestones.title: Reject impossible work
actions: Check the exact boundary where all messages are answered.

milestones.title: Explain rejection
actions: Describe which input rule was broken.
Keep the priority rule separate from validation.

acceptance: Text, fractions, and negative counts are rejected.
Too many answered messages are rejected.
The exact valid boundary is tested.
project.extension: Add a separate message describing the first validation problem. Keep the result vocabulary unchanged.
reflection: Why should validation happen before routing?
How would the interface explain invalid input?
